# 3. The questionnaire

<!-- generated by tools/render_docs.py - do not edit by hand -->

Questionnaire version **1.0.0**, effective 2026-01-01. Review cycle: **12 months** (Art. 54(13) DR 2017/565, ESMA GL5).

Scores in brackets are the option's contribution to its dimension before weighting. A `*` marks the correct answer to an objective comprehension item. Questions marked *cross-check only* carry no weight and exist to detect over-estimation (ESMA GL4 paras 46, 52).

## Design rules

1. No question asks the client to certify their own suitability or to pick their own risk level (GL1 para 14).
2. Self-declared knowledge is never scored (GL4 para 46).
3. Loss questions are shown with the equivalent monetary amount (GL4 para 48).
4. Sustainability preferences are collected separately and applied only after the Art. 25(2) assessment (GL8 para 81).
5. No answer that widens the product range is made easier to give than one that narrows it (Art. 55(2)).

## Section A - Client, mandate and personal circumstances

Not scored.

> DR 2017/565 Art. 54(2), 54(6)
> ESMA GL2 para 24 (marital status, family situation, age, employment, liquidity needs)
> ESMA GL6 (legal entities and groups)

**A1.** Client categorisation for this mandate.

`type: single` · `required`

- Retail client
- Elective professional client
- Per se professional client

**A2.** Who is being assessed?

`type: single` · `required`

> Where the client is a legal person or a group, the firm's policy under ESMA GL6 determines whose knowledge, financial situation and objectives are used. Profiles are never averaged (GL6 para 70).

- A single natural person
- Two or more natural persons (no legal representative)
- A natural person represented by another natural person
- A legal person

**A3.** Service being provided.

`type: single` · `required`

- Investment advice (instrument by instrument)
- Investment advice on a portfolio basis
- Discretionary portfolio management

**A4.** Age of the client (or of the underlying client whose objectives govern).

`type: numeric` · `required`


**A5.** Employment situation.

`type: single` · `required`

- Employed, permanent contract
- Employed, fixed-term or variable income
- Self-employed / business owner
- Retired
- Not currently working
- Student

**A6.** Marital status and financial dependants.

`type: single` · `required`

- Single, no dependants
- Married / partnered, no dependants
- 1-2 financial dependants
- 3 or more financial dependants

**A7.** Do any of the following apply?

`type: multi` · `required`

> Indicators of client vulnerability trigger a more in-depth information requirement and a prudence overlay (ESMA GL3 para 40).

- None of the following
- This portfolio is or will become the client's main source of income
- Retirement expected within 5 years
- Assets arise from a one-off event (inheritance, sale of business, settlement)
- First-time investor in financial instruments
- Advice is not being given in the client's first language

## Section B - Knowledge and experience

Scored. Feeds the **knowledge** dimension.

> MiFID II Art. 25(2)
> DR 2017/565 Art. 54(2)(c); Art. 55(1)(a)-(c)
> ESMA GL2 paras 30-31; GL4 paras 46, 52

**B0.** How would you describe your own knowledge of investing? *(cross-check only, not scored)*

`type: single` · `required`

> Not used to compute the knowledge score. Retained solely to detect over-estimation against the objective items B5-B10 (GL4 para 52).

- None  <sub>self_rating 1</sub>
- Basic  <sub>self_rating 2</sub>
- Good  <sub>self_rating 3</sub>
- Advanced  <sub>self_rating 4</sub>
- Professional  <sub>self_rating 5</sub>

**B1.** Education and professional background relevant to financial markets.

**B2.** Which of the following have you personally invested in, and understood at the time?

**B3.** Over the last three years, how many investment transactions have you carried out?

`type: single` · `required`

- 21-50 in total  <sub>score 80</sub>

**B4.** Typical size of a single transaction over that period.

`type: single` · `required`

`type: single` · `required`

`type: single` · `required`

- A higher expected return can be obtained without any increase in possible loss

`type: single` · `required`

## Section D - Investment objectives and horizon

Scored. Feeds the **objective** dimension.

> DR 2017/565 Art. 54(2)(a); Art. 54(5) - length of time, purposes of the investment
> ESMA GL3 para 42 - multiple or long-term objectives require more detail

**D1.** Primary purpose of this investment.

`type: single` · `required`

- Protect the nominal value of the capital  <sub>objective_band 1</sub>
- Keep pace with inflation with very limited fluctuation  <sub>objective_band 2</sub>
- Generate a regular income stream  <sub>objective_band 2</sub>
- Balance growth and stability over the medium term  <sub>objective_band 3</sub>
- Grow capital over the long term, accepting significant fluctuation  <sub>objective_band 4</sub>
- Maximise long-term growth, accepting large losses along the way  <sub>objective_band 5</sub>

**D2.** For how long do you intend to hold this investment?

`type: single` · `required`

- Less than 2 years  <sub>horizon_band 1, horizon_years 1</sub>
- 2 to 3 years  <sub>horizon_band 2, horizon_years 3</sub>
- 3 to 5 years  <sub>horizon_band 2, horizon_years 5</sub>
- 5 to 7 years  <sub>horizon_band 3, horizon_years 7</sub>
- 7 to 10 years  <sub>horizon_band 4, horizon_years 10</sub>
- More than 10 years  <sub>horizon_band 5, horizon_years 15</sub>

**D3.** Is the money tied to a specific future commitment?

`type: single` · `required`

- No specific commitment  <sub>score 100</sub>
- Yes, but the date is flexible  <sub>score 70</sub>
- Yes, on a fixed date (property purchase, education, retirement)  <sub>score 30</sub>

**D4.** Do you intend to draw regular withdrawals during the holding period?

`type: single` · `required`

- No withdrawals  <sub>score 100</sub>
- Yes, up to 3% of the portfolio per year  <sub>score 70</sub>
- Yes, 3% - 5% per year  <sub>score 45</sub>
- Yes, more than 5% per year  <sub>score 10</sub>

**D5.** Which return expectation is closest to yours for this portfolio, over the horizon you gave?

`type: single` · `required`

> Used as a reality check against the risk level the client is willing to accept. An expectation materially above what the accepted risk level can plausibly deliver is a documented inconsistency (GL4 para 51).

- Around 1-2% a year  <sub>implied_band 1</sub>
- Around 2-4% a year  <sub>implied_band 2</sub>
- Around 4-6% a year  <sub>implied_band 3</sub>
- Around 6-9% a year  <sub>implied_band 4</sub>
- More than 9% a year  <sub>implied_band 5</sub>

**D6.** Do you have other goals for other pools of money that this portfolio does not cover?

`type: boolean` · `required`

Scored. Feeds the **tolerance** dimension.

**E1.** Five portfolios of EUR 100,000 are shown with their plausible value after one year in a good and in a bad year. Which would you choose?

`type: single` · `required`

- Best EUR 108,000 / Worst EUR 93,000  <sub>score 25</sub>
- Best EUR 116,000 / Worst EUR 85,000  <sub>score 50</sub>
- Best EUR 126,000 / Worst EUR 74,000  <sub>score 75</sub>
- Best EUR 138,000 / Worst EUR 62,000  <sub>score 100</sub>

`type: single` · `required`

- Sell everything and move to cash  <sub>score 0</sub>
- Sell part of it to limit further loss  <sub>score 25</sub>
- Do nothing and wait for recovery  <sub>score 65</sub>
- Do nothing, but review whether my plan still holds  <sub>score 75</sub>
- Invest more while prices are lower  <sub>score 100</sub>

**E3.** What is the largest fall in the value of this portfolio, over twelve months, that you would accept without changing your plan?

`type: single` · `required`

- No fall at all  <sub>score 0, tolerance_loss_pct 0</sub>
- Up to 5%  <sub>score 20, tolerance_loss_pct 5</sub>
- Up to 10%  <sub>score 40, tolerance_loss_pct 10</sub>
- Up to 20%  <sub>score 65, tolerance_loss_pct 20</sub>
- Up to 35%  <sub>score 85, tolerance_loss_pct 35</sub>
- More than 35%  <sub>score 100, tolerance_loss_pct 45</sub>

**E4.** Have you previously held investments through a market fall of 20% or more (for example 2008, 2020 or 2022)?

`type: single` · `required`

> Observed past behaviour is weighted more heavily than stated attitude (GL4 para 46).

- I was not invested at the time
- Yes - I sold at a loss  <sub>score 0</sub>
- Yes - I reduced my exposure  <sub>score 30</sub>
- Yes - I held my position  <sub>score 75</sub>
- Yes - I added to my position  <sub>score 100</sub>

**E5.** Which statement is closest to your view?

`type: single` · `required`

- Avoiding any loss matters more to me than growth  <sub>score 0</sub>
- I want mainly stability, with a little growth  <sub>score 25</sub>
- I accept moderate ups and downs for moderate growth  <sub>score 50</sub>
- I accept substantial ups and downs for higher long-term growth  <sub>score 75</sub>
- I am comfortable with large losses in pursuit of the highest return  <sub>score 100</sub>

## Section F - Sustainability preferences

Not scored.
Applied only after the Art. 25(2) assessment is complete.

> DR 2017/565 Art. 2(7)(a)-(c); Art. 54(2)(a), 54(5), 54(9), 54(10)
> ESMA GL2 paras 26-29; GL8 paras 81-85, 88

**F1.** Do you have sustainability preferences for this portfolio?

`type: single` · `required`

> Explained to the client in non-technical terms before the question is put (GL1 para 16). Answering "no" makes the client sustainability-neutral; products with and without sustainability features may then be recommended (GL8 para 85).

- No preference
- Yes
- Yes, but I do not know which aspects matter to me

**F2.** Which aspects should apply?

`type: multi` · `conditional`
 · shown when F1 in ['yes', 'undecided']

- A minimum proportion invested in environmentally sustainable activities under the Taxonomy Regulation
- A minimum proportion invested in sustainable investments under the SFDR
- That principal adverse impacts on sustainability factors are considered

**F3.** Minimum proportion for the aspects you selected.

`type: single` · `conditional`
 · shown when F2 in ['taxonomy', 'sfdr_sustainable']

> Standardised minimum proportions are permitted (GL2 para 27).

- At least 10%  <sub>min_proportion 0.1</sub>
- At least 25%  <sub>min_proportion 0.25</sub>
- At least 50%  <sub>min_proportion 0.5</sub>
- At least 75%  <sub>min_proportion 0.75</sub>

**F4.** Which categories of adverse impact should be considered?

`type: multi` · `conditional`
 · shown when F2 in ['pai']

> Categories rather than individual indicators may be used (GL2 para 27).

- Climate and other environment-related impacts
- Social and employee matters
- Respect for human rights
- Anti-corruption and anti-bribery

**F5.** What share of this portfolio should meet your sustainability preferences?

`type: single` · `conditional`
 · shown when F1 in ['yes', 'undecided']

- At least 25% of the portfolio  <sub>portfolio_share 0.25</sub>
- At least 50% of the portfolio  <sub>portfolio_share 0.5</sub>
- At least 75% of the portfolio  <sub>portfolio_share 0.75</sub>
- The whole portfolio  <sub>portfolio_share 1.0</sub>
